text:
Simon Holmstrom's month went from a fourth-line demotion to his first NHL hat trick, three goals in a 6-2 win at Anaheim, as Stefen Rosner of NHL.com put it. He is on a four-game point streak with five goals and three assists, and has 15 points in 19 games.

Plenty of this is real. He is playing 18:18 a night, up from 16:44, and he is on the ice for 46% of the Islanders' power-play chances, up from 19% last season. His own chances are up too, 0.97 expected goals per 60 from 0.66. The Islanders control the five-on-five game with him on the ice, at 53% of expected goals.

The finishing is the part that won't hold. He has nine goals on 5.6 expected, shooting 25% against 19% last season, and his team has scored 4.3 more than expected with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries last season, the kind of habit that keeps chances coming when the shots stop dropping. Nineteen games is a small sample, and Rosner already has his next contract on the table.
headline: From the fourth line to a hat trick
